page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top: page number left, running title right. Two coin illustrations at top centre (no text block). Below them one column of running text, full width, then one short paragraph below. No margin notes.

main_text.head: MAGNENTIVS, Comes duorum ordinum Augustæ (vrbs est Germaniæ) cōuiuiū militibus exhibuit, à mane ad vesperam, more gentis. inde in cubiculū ingressus, statim egressus est, indutus purpura, ac multis satellitibus cinctus: qui cōscij non erat, coacti sunt assentiri: donatiuum dedit, posuitq; custodes ne quis rem aperiret. deinde cum lectissimis Gaisone mittit, qui Constantem in tentorio occidit, anno mundi 4313. à Christo nato 351. Hic Cæsare facit Decentium fratrem, mittitq; cum exercitu vti Gallias tueatur iamq; tota Italia: & Africa Magnentij erant. Constātius tunc in Oriente aduersam fortunam cōtra Persas experiebatur: ad quē legatos misit cum literis, vti Oriēte & Thraciis cōtentus esset: qui nihil respondet, sed Gallum patruelem Cæsarē faciēs, eum in Oriēte relinquit: ipse Hesperios adit, vlturus fratris cædē. attamen ne sua Roma bello vexaretur ciuili Gallia Magnentio permittit, si arma deponat: Tyrānus sperans vincere, non paruit. pugnatur ad Mursam, magnis vtrinque viribus: vincitur Magnentius: bellū reparat: victus iterum, tandem gladio occultè prouisso mortem sibi consciscit. Pom. Læ. in Constāte. Aurel. Victo. Hic Desiderium fratrem per furorem vulnerauit, & quosdam ex amicis occidit, paulò ante quàm seipsum occideret.
main_text.p: DECENTIVS qui Gallias tuebatur, audito fratris sui Magnentij casu, laqueo apud Senonas vitam finiuit, sibi metuens. horum frater Desiderius Constantiū adiit, à quo humanissimè exceptus est anno mundi 4316. à Christo nato 354. Pomp. Læt. Aurel. Vict.

page.notes: Two coin portraits (illustrations, not text): left reads "D N MAGNENTIVS P F AVG", right reads "D N DECENTIVS NOB CAES". Small specks near the text are not printed text. Printing errors left as printed: "Gaisone", "Constātius" spelled as printed. Heading styling: the opening words "MAGNENTIVS" and "DECENTIVS" are in capitals and set apart; the first is larger, so it is shown as a line-leading heading with the rest of the paragraph text inside it. The first paragraph was set as a single block in the scan; its later paragraph break is not visible, so it is kept as one paragraph.
